added_meaning: The Senate 90005(b) State Border Security Reinforcement Fund is a distinct DHS fund. Its complete selected operative clauses are retained below. Senate 90005(b) paragraph 1: There is established, in the Department of Homeland Security, a fund to be known as the ``State Border Security Reinforcement Fund.'' Senate 90005(b) paragraph 2: The Secretary of Homeland Security shall use amounts appropriated or otherwise made available for the Fund for grants to eligible States and units of local government for any of the following purposes: Senate 90005(b) purpose A: Construction or installation of a border wall, border fencing or other barrier, or buoys along the southern border of the United States, which may include planning, procurement of materials, and personnel costs related to such construction or installation. Senate 90005(b) purpose B: Any work necessary to prepare the ground at or near land borders to allow construction and maintenance of a border wall or other barrier fencing. Senate 90005(b) purpose C: Detection and interdiction of illicit substances and aliens who have unlawfully entered the United States and have committed a crime under Federal, State, or local law, and transfer or referral of such aliens to the Department of Homeland Security as provided by law. Senate 90005(b) purpose D: Relocation of aliens who are unlawfully present in the United States from small population centers to other domestic locations. Senate 90005(b) paragraph 3: In addition to amounts otherwise available for the purposes described in paragraph (2), there is appropriated for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to the Department of Homeland Security for the State Border Security Reinforcement Fund established by paragraph (1), $10,000,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2034, for qualified expenses for such purposes. Senate 90005(b) paragraph 4: The Secretary of Homeland Security may provide grants from the fund established by paragraph (1) to State agencies and units of local governments for expenditures made for completed, ongoing, or new activities, in accordance with law, that occurred on or after January 20, 2021. Senate 90005(b) paragraph 5: Each State desiring to apply for a grant under this subsection shall submit an application to the Secretary containing such information in support of the application as the Secretary may require. The Secretary shall require that each State include in its application the purposes for which the State seeks the funds and a description of how the State plans to allocate the funds. The Secretary shall begin to accept applications not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act. Senate 90005(b) paragraph 6: Nothing in this subsection shall authorize any State or local government to exercise immigration or border security authorities reserved exclusively to the Federal Government under the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1101 et seq.) or the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 101 et seq.). The Federal Emergency Management Agency may use not more than 1 percent of the funds made available under this subsection for the purpose of administering grants provided for in this section. The paragraph (2)(C) alien category retains both unlawful entry and commission of a crime under Federal, State, or local law; those alien predicates do not classify illicit substances. Transfer or referral remains as provided by law. Paragraph (2)(D) instead concerns unlawful presence and relocation from small population centers to other domestic locations; it does not borrow the crime or unlawful-entry predicates from (C), or authorize an international return. Only (A) specifies the southern border; (B) says at or near land borders. The paragraph (2) eligible-State/local-unit grant purpose rule and paragraph (4) discretionary State-agency/local-government expenditure rule remain distinct. The paragraph (5) application obligations name each State; no additional local-government obligation is inferred. The 90-day clause concerns when the Secretary must begin accepting applications, not an applicant deadline or a finding that applications are open. The paragraph (6) construction rule preserves exclusively Federal authorities without deciding which actual functions or expenditures fall within that reservation. The FEMA administration ceiling is discretionary, no more than 1 percent of funds under this subsection for grants in this section; its two scope words remain distinct. This is not an actual award, expenditure, eligibility, individual status/crime, relocation, power delegation or reimbursement determination. House reimbursement amounts, availability, January 21 date and duplicate-reimbursement restriction are not imported. Other package components and the 51 separately reserved application questions remain unfinished.
